title_en: Zeng Yilong v. Jiangxi Jinma Auction Co., Ltd., Bank of China Co., Ltd., Shangrao Branch, and Xu Shengju — auction dispute
ruling_gist_en: In accordance with the relevant provisions of the Contract Law and the Auction Law, an auction is a transaction method in which specific items or property rights are transferred to the highest bidder through public bidding. Auction activities must comply with legal provisions and industry practices and must conform to the principles of fairness and justice. In an auction activity, if an auctioneer's conduct violates legal provisions and industry practices and infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a bidder, the auction shall be deemed invalid.

full_text_en:
Zeng Yilong v. Jiangxi Jinma Auction Co., Ltd., 
Bank of China Co., Ltd. Shangrao Branch, 
and Xu Shengju — Auction Dispute

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Contract Law and the Auction Law, an auction is a method of sale in which a specific item or property right is transferred to the highest bidder through open competitive bidding. Auction activities must comply with legal provisions and industry practices, and must conform to the principles of fairness and justice. Where, during an auction, the auctioneer's conduct violates legal provisions and industry customary practices, and infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of relevant bidders, such auction conduct shall be deemed invalid.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2005) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 43

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Zeng Yilong, male, Han nationality, born on October 29, 1958, businessman, residing at No. 130 Banyun New Village, Shangrao City, Jiangxi Province.

Appointed Agent: Qu Songping, lawyer of Beijing Xinyi Law Firm.

Appointed Agent: Chen Chen, lawyer of Beijing Xinyi Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Jiangxi Jinma Auction Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 63 Daihu Road, Xinzhou District, Shangrao City, Jiangxi Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Yibo, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Appointed Agent: Gong Zhizhong, lawyer of Beijing Jiarun Law Firm.

Appointed Agent: Tian Tao, male, Han nationality, born on October 2, 1946, Director of the Legal Consultation and Theoretical Research Committee of the China Association of Auctioneers, residing at No. 12 Jiaochang Er Tiao, Xuanwu District, Beijing.

Third Party at First Instance: Bank of China Co., Ltd. Shangrao Branch, domiciled at No. 43 Shengli Road, Xinzhou District, Shangrao City, Jiangxi Province.

Person in Charge: Zhong Dingli, Branch Manager.

Appointed Agent: Li Zhiyong, lawyer of Jiangxi Dijing Law Firm.

Appointed Agent: Wang Hualan, lawyer of Jiangxi Dijing Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Xu Shengju, male, Han nationality, born on November 21, 1941, Legal Representative of Shangrao Huashang Economic and Trade Industrial Co., Ltd., residing at No. 36 Shengli Road, Xinzhou District, Shangrao City, Jiangxi Province.

Appointed Agent: Xu Wei, male, Han nationality, born on February 28, 1967, official of the United Front Work Department of the CPC Shangrao Municipal Committee, residing at Room 501, No. 5 Yanhe Middle Road, Shangrao City, Jiangxi Province.

Appointed Agent: Liu Jianmin, male, Han nationality, born on July 27, 1973, Legal Adviser of Shangrao Huashang Economic and Trade Industrial Co., Ltd., residing at Room 702, Unit A, Building 35, Shiji Garden, Xinzhou District, Shangrao City, Jiangxi Province.

The appellant Zeng Yilong, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2004) Gan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 4 rendered by the Jiangxi High People's Court in the case of dispute over auction with the appellee Jiangxi Jinma Auction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinma Company), the third party at first instance Bank of China Co., Ltd. Shangrao Branch (hereinafter referred to as BOC Shangrao Branch), and Xu Shengju, appealed to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and heard the case on June 21, 2005. The appellant Zeng Yilong and his appointed agents Qu Songping and Chen Chen, the appointed agents of the appellee Jinma Company Gong Zhizhong and Tian Tao, the appointed agents of the third party at first instance BOC Shangrao Branch Li Zhiyong and Wang Hualan, and the appointed agents of the third party at first instance Xu Shengju, Xu Wei and Liu Jianmin, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case has now been concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial that: BOC Shangrao Branch, pursuant to the civil ruling (2003) Rao Zhong Zhi Zi No. 35 rendered by the Shangrao Intermediate People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Shangrao Intermediate Court) on December 24, 2003, entrusted Jinma Company to auction in its entirety the property located at the "Zhengda Commercial Building" in Shangrao City, from the basement to the fourth floor, with a total construction area of approximately 62,896 square meters. After accepting the entrustment, Jinma Company published an auction announcement in the Shangrao Daily on April 29, 2004, which stated that the auction of the "Zhengda Commercial Building" and other real estate would be held in the afternoon of May 12, 2004, the auctioneer in charge would be the nationally registered auctioneer Ye Qing, the starting bid for the subject matter was RMB 20 million, the auction method was an ascending price auction with a reserve price, and also set out the registration procedures for bidders. Subsequently, Zeng Yilong, Xu Shengju, and the lessee Shangrao Huashang Economic and Trade Industrial Co., Ltd., among six bidders, completed the bidder registration procedures in accordance with the announcement. Zeng Yilong and Xu Shengju each paid a deposit of RMB 2 million and obtained bidding paddles No. 12 and No. 17 respectively. Zeng Yilong was in partnership with Xu Xiaoming, Yu Jianming, Zhan Shouxing, Liu Zhihua, and Zhu Weiqiang, and was elected by the partners as the holder of paddle No. 12. Xu Wei, entrusted by Xu Shengju, acted as his agent for bidding matters.

The auction of the "Zhengda Commercial Building" was held at 5:00 p.m. on May 12, 2004, presided over by auctioneer Ye Qing. Ye Qing introduced the situation of the "Zhengda Commercial Building" to the bidders, then announced that the bidding for the "Zhengda Commercial Building" had commenced, with a starting bid of RMB 20 million and increments of no less than RMB 500,000. After Ye Qing called the bid at RMB 20.5 million and announced "RMB 20.5 million, first call," Zeng Yilong raised his paddle and bid RMB 21 million. Thereafter, Ye Qing called the bid at RMB 21 million three times, and seeing no response, informed Zeng Yilong that his bid had not reached the reserve price of RMB 26.7 million, and asked Zeng Yilong whether he would accept the reserve price of RMB 26.7 million. Zeng Yilong raised his paddle to bid, whereupon Ye Qing immediately brought down the gavel and announced that Zeng Yilong had won the property rights of the building part of the "Zhengda Commercial Building" at RMB 26.7 million. At this point, bidder No. 17, Xu Wei, questioned Ye Qing's operation, arguing that he should have conducted a full round of bidding at the price of RMB 26.7 million. Subsequently, bidder No. 21, Xu Shengju, and bidder No. 16 (the accountant of Shangrao Huashang Economic and Trade Industrial Co., Ltd.) also accused Ye Qing of not calling three times at the price of RMB 26.7 million and not asking whether anyone would increase the bid. Zeng Yilong said: "The auction has already concluded with the gavel; there is no further increase." Ye Qing also explained that he had already called three times at the price of RMB 21 million. Xu Shengju repeatedly raised objections, while Xu Wei demanded that Ye Qing re-auction. Under these circumstances, Ye Qing stated: "RMB 26.7 million was the paddle raised by No. 12. If you want to increase above RMB 26.7 million, you may do so, but at RMB 21 million you have no right." Zeng Yilong protested: "If you re-auction, I disagree." Bidder No. 16 said: "Auctioneer, you must announce three times before we accept it." Ye Qing said: "If someone bids higher after the final bid, that is permissible." Thereafter, Ye Qing ignored Zeng Yilong's reminder that he had already brought down the gavel, and continued the auction starting from RMB 26.7 million, successively adjusting the increment to RMB 100,000 and RMB 50,000. Zeng Yilong initially threw down his paddle in protest, but when Ye Qing called the bid at RMB 27.15 million, he raised his paddle to bid. Subsequently, bidder No. 16 raised his paddle to bid RMB 27.2 million. Seeing this, Zeng Yilong asked the on-site supervisory personnel to intervene, but to no avail, and then declared that he had already won the bid at RMB 26.7 million and reserved that right. Ye Qing continued to preside over the auction after giving some explanations to Zeng Yilong. Finally, after bidder No. 17 raised his paddle to bid RMB 27.4 million and Ye Qing called three times, seeing no further paddle raised, he brought down the gavel and announced that bidder No. 17 had won the partial property rights of the "Zhengda Commercial Building" at RMB 27.4 million. Ye Qing and Xu Wei immediately signed the Auction Meeting Record. At the same time, Jinma Company filled out an Auction Transaction Confirmation Form, which stated that the subject matter of the auction was the real estate from the basement to the fourth floor of the "Zhengda Commercial Building," the auction transaction price was RMB 27.4 million, the auction commission was 5% of the auction transaction price, and also specified the time for payment of the auction price and commission. Xu Wei signed the form.

On May 13, 2004, Zeng Yilong and his partners Xu Xiaoming, Yu Jianming, Zhan Shouxing, Liu Zhihua, and Zhu Weiqiang sent a letter to Jinma Company, stating that the auction conduct between Jinma Company and bidder No. 17 was invalid, and requesting the company to immediately cease handling the purchase procedures for bidder No. 17. On May 26 of the same year, Zeng Yilong and his partners again sent a letter to Jinma Company, stating that they had won the partial property rights of the "Zhengda Commercial Building" at RMB 26.7 million at the auction on May 12, 2004, and requesting the company to assist in handling the auction transaction confirmation letter and property title transfer procedures. After receiving the above two official letters, Jinma Company did not reply. On June 11, 2004, Jinma Company deposited the RMB 2 million deposit paid by Zeng Yilong with the Xinzhou District Notary Office of Shangrao City, which on the same day served a Notice of Receipt of Deposited Property on Zeng Yilong, requiring Zeng Yilong to collect the RMB 2 million deposit deposited by Jinma Company before July 11, 2004; otherwise, the money would be turned over to the state treasury. On July 22, 2004, Zeng Yilong submitted an Application to Jinma Company, again requesting the company to handle the auction transaction-related procedures for him. Jinma Company did not respond to this, so Zeng Yilong filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance.

Zeng Yilong alleged: On the afternoon of May 12, 2004, he held bidding paddle No. 12 and participated in the auction presided over by Jinma Company. After the auctioneer brought down the gavel and announced that bidder No. 12 had won the bid at RMB 26.7 million, because other bidders raised objections, the auctioneer actually made another bid and announced that the subject matter (partial property rights of the basement and the first to fourth floors of the "Zhengda Commercial Building") was won by bidder No. 17. During the subsequent illegal auction process, he repeatedly protested to no avail. Thereafter, he repeatedly contacted Jinma Company, but the company insisted on handling the transaction procedures for bidder No. 17. Therefore, he requested the court to order Jinma Company to immediately issue a transaction confirmation letter for the partial property rights of the basement and the first to fourth floors of the "Zhengda Commercial Building" (bidding price RMB 26.7 million), and to order Jinma Company to bear all litigation costs. On October 28, 2004, Zeng Yilong amended his claims as follows: 1. A judgment confirming that the second gavel strike (bidding price RMB 27.4 million) for the subject matter by Jinma Company was invalid; 2. A judgment confirming that the first gavel strike (bidding price RMB 26.7 million) for the subject matter by Jinma Company was valid; 3. Revoking the Auction Transaction Confirmation Form signed by Jinma Company with Xu Wei on May 12, 2004; 4. Ordering Jinma Company to immediately issue a transaction confirmation letter for the partial property rights of the basement and the first to fourth floors of the "Zhengda Commercial Building" at a price of RMB 26.7 million. Jinma Company was to bear all litigation costs of this case.

In support of his claims, Zeng Yilong provided the following evidence: 1. The auction announcement published by Jinma Company in the Shangrao Daily on April 29, 2004; 2. The Auction Rules, Auction Lot List, and Special Provisions provided by Jinma Company to each bidder; 3. The Receipt issued by Jinma Company after receiving the RMB 2 million deposit from Zeng Yilong; 4. The video recording of the auction site and a written description of the audiovisual material; 5. The letters sent by Zeng Yilong and his partners to Jinma Company on May 13, 2004, and May 26, 2004, respectively; 6. The Notice of Receipt of Deposited Property issued to Zeng Yilong by the Xinzhou District Notary Office of Shangrao City on June 11, 2004; 7. The Expert Opinion issued by the Commercial Law Research Society of the China Law Society; 8. The Application submitted by Zeng Yilong to Jinma Company on July 22, 2004.

Jinma Company argued in its defense: Zeng Yilong did not lawfully win the subject matter, and the company was not required to issue a property transaction confirmation letter for him. The reasons were: 1. Before the reserve price of the subject matter in this case was announced, Zeng Yilong's highest bid was an invalid offer; 2. The company's auctioneer's act of bringing down the gavel for Zeng Yilong's transaction at the reserve price was improper, infringing upon the legitimate rights of other bidders, especially the lessee. The auctioneer's timely correction of the erroneous conduct was in accordance with legal provisions; 3. The lessee won the transaction at the highest bid of RMB 27.4 million and signed a transaction confirmation letter. This auction conduct was lawful and valid.

Jinma Company provided the following evidence: 1. The reply letter Zhongpai Xie Han Zi [2004] No. 14 from the China Association of Auctioneers to Jinma Company; 2. The Auction Meeting Record prepared by Jinma Company; 3. The Auction Transaction Confirmation Form of Jinma Company signed and acknowledged by Xu Wei; 4. A CD of the auction site (Jinma Company acknowledged that this evidence was the same as evidence 4 provided by Zeng Yilong, so no written description was attached).

Because Jinma Company argued that the subject matter in this case was sold to the lessee Shangrao Huashang Economic and Trade Industrial Co., Ltd. at the highest bid of RMB 27.4 million, while the Auction Transaction Confirmation Form of Jinma Company was signed with Xu Wei. To ascertain the facts, the court of first instance ex officio obtained the registration materials of bidder No. 17, including: 1. Jinma Company's Bidder Registration Form; 2. Jinma Company's Bidder Qualification Certificate; 3. The Power of Attorney written by Xu Shengju; 4. A copy of Xu Shengju's identity card; 5. A copy of Xu Wei's identity card. Upon review of the above evidence, the court of first instance confirmed that bidder No. 17 was Xu Shengju (Legal Representative of Shangrao Huashang Economic and Trade Industrial Co., Ltd.), and Xu Wei was the agent of Xu Shengju. Given that the party entrusting Jinma Company to auction the subject matter in this case was BOC Shangrao Branch, and Jinma Company had already signed an Auction Transaction Confirmation Form with Xu Wei, the agent of Xu Shengju, before Zeng Yilong filed the lawsuit, the outcome of this case had legal interests for BOC Shangrao Branch and Xu Shengju. Therefore, on November 18, 2004, the court of first instance notified BOC Shangrao Branch and Xu Shengju to participate in the proceedings as third parties, and the parties had no objection to this.

After the third party at first instance, BOC Shangrao Branch, participated in the proceedings, it did not make a specific defense during the first instance but provided the following evidence to prove that it was the rights holder of the subject matter in this case: 1. The civil ruling (2003) Rao Zhong Zhi Zi No. 35 of the Shangrao Intermediate Court; 2. The Loan Real Estate Mortgage Contract (2001) Rao Fang Di Di Ya Zi No. 319.

The third party at first instance, Xu Shengju, argued in his first instance defense: 1. The auctioneer's act of immediately declaring invalid the gavel strike on Zeng Yilong's bid during the auction was lawful and proper; 2. Zeng Yilong's claim requested the court to let the auctioneer's error stand, which should not be supported; 3. Continuing the auction after the gavel strike to correct the error did not violate the principle of "the gavel strike finalizes the deal"; 4. This case should be stayed. The reason was that the Shangrao Intermediate Court had already accepted a lawsuit filed by the lessee Shangrao Huashang Economic and Trade Industrial Co., Ltd., the facts and reasons of which were that the transfer of the property in this case by agreement between the lessor Jiangxi Shangrao Commercial (Group) Co., Ltd. and BOC Shangrao Branch on December 9, 2003, infringed upon the right of first refusal of Shangrao Huashang Economic and Trade Industrial Co., Ltd. This case concerned the validity of the gavel strike at the auction on May 12, 2004. The former case took precedence over the latter, so this case should be stayed.

The court of first instance also found: The Auction Rules of the auction provided by Jinma Company to the bidders participating in this auction stated in Article 8: The auction must be presided over by the auctioneer, who has the right to adjust the bid increment. The bid of a bidder shall not be less than the bid increment prescribed by the auctioneer. Once a bid is made, it cannot be withdrawn. When another bidder makes a higher bid, the previous bid loses its binding effect. When the highest bid of a bidder is confirmed by the auctioneer's gavel, the auction is concluded, and the bidder making the highest bid becomes the buyer; Article 9: If the auction subject has a reserve price, and the highest bid of a bidder does not reach the reserve price, such bid is invalid, and the auctioneer has the right to stop the auction of that subject; Article 10: After the auction is concluded, the buyer must immediately sign Jinma Company's Auction Transaction Confirmation Form and the auction record, pay the full auction price and auction commission within the specified time, and sign the transaction confirmation letter.

During the first instance of this case, the Shangrao Intermediate Court accepted a case of a lease contract dispute filed by Shangrao Huashang Economic and Trade Industrial Co., Ltd. against Jiangxi Shangrao Commercial (Group) Co., Ltd., in which Zeng Yilong and BOC Shangrao Branch were both listed as third parties. On February 3, 2005, Shangrao Huashang Economic and Trade Industrial Co., Ltd. applied for withdrawal of the lawsuit, and the Shangrao Intermediate Court issued the civil ruling (2004) Rao Zhong Min Yi Chu Zi No. 13 on February 4, 2005, permitting the withdrawal.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence that has been examined in court at first instance: 1. The civil ruling (2003) Rao Zhong Zhi Zi No. 35 of the Shangrao Intermediate Court; 2. Jinma Company's Auction Announcement and Auction Rules; 3. The Receipt issued by Jinma Company after receiving the RMB 2 million deposit from Zeng Yilong; 4. Relevant materials of Xu Shengju's participation in the auction registration; 5. The video recording of the auction site and a written description of the audiovisual material; 6. Jinma Company's Auction Meeting Record and Auction Transaction Confirmation Form; 7. The two letters from Zeng Yilong and his partners to Jinma Company; 8. The Notice of Receipt of Deposited Property from the Xinzhou District Notary Office of Shangrao City; 9. The Application submitted by Zeng Yilong to Jinma Company. The parties have no objection to the above facts, and the court of first instance confirms them.

The court of first instance held that the method of auction for the subject matter in this case was an ascending price auction with a reserve price. Article 28 of the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The principal has the right to determine the reserve price of the auction subject matter and require the auctioneer to keep it confidential." Although the existing evidence cannot reflect whether the Shangrao Branch of Bank of China requested that the reserve price be kept confidential at all times, when the auctioneer disclosed the reserve price during the auction process, the representative of the Shangrao Branch of Bank of China present at the site did not express any objection. After the branch joined the lawsuit as a third party, it also did not raise any objection to the auctioneer's conduct. This should be deemed as its failure to make such a request. Therefore, the auctioneer's act of disclosing the reserve price based on the circumstances at the site did not violate the law. At the beginning of this auction, the highest bid from the bidders was RMB 21 million, which did not reach the reserve price of RMB 26.7 million. According to Article 50 of the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China, if the highest bid does not reach the reserve price, that bid is invalid and the auctioneer shall stop the auction of the subject matter. Accordingly, Jinma Company's auctioneer should have stopped the auction. However, in auction practice, there are situations where, after the auctioneer discloses the reserve price, the auction continues because the principal has not orally or in writing informed the auctioneer of the intention to let the auction fail. Therefore, the validity of subsequent auction actions cannot be denied simply because the auctioneer did not stop the auction. To examine whether the auctioneer's first hammer fall was proper, it must first be determined whether the auctioneer's quotation of the reserve price constituted a bidding quotation and whether three quotations were required. In this case, although Zeng Yilong's bid of RMB 21 million was the highest quotation at the time of the auction, according to Article 50 of the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China, that bid did not take effect because it did not reach the reserve price of RMB 26.7 million. Since Zeng Yilong's bid was invalid, in the subsequent auction activities presided over by the auctioneer, he was in an equal position with other bidders and did not have the right to purchase directly at the reserve price. Therefore, the auctioneer's quotation of the reserve price constituted a bidding quotation and should have solicited whether any bidder had a higher bid. As to whether three quotations were required, the evidence shows that the "three-call quotation method" used at the auction site is a customary technical measure in China's auction market, for which there are no specific provisions in the relevant laws. In this auction, although Jinma Company's Auction Rules and the auctioneer's emphasis on precautions did not mention the quotation method, the auctioneer used the "three-call quotation method" in the earlier stage of the auction, indicating that he recognized this technical measure and had reached an agreement with the bidders on this matter. Therefore, the auctioneer should still have made three quotations in the subsequent auction activities. When the highest bid at the site did not reach the reserve price, the auctioneer of Jinma Company, for the benefit of the principal, disclosed the reserve price and continued to preside over the auction. This actually initiated a new round of bidding, and the previous highest bid became invalid. However, the auctioneer misunderstood Article 50 of the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 9 of Jinma Company's Auction Rules, mistakenly believing that other bidders who did not bid at the RMB 21 million price had lost their bidding rights for the auction subject matter. Consequently, without fulfilling the obligation of notification, he inquired solely of Zeng Yilong, made only one quotation, and then dropped the hammer to declare the auction concluded. This conduct violated the basic principles of the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China, infringed on the interests of other bidders, and also failed to maximize the principal's interests. Therefore, this hammer fall by the auctioneer was clearly improper. Subsequently, due to objections from other bidders, the auctioneer recognized his mistake and resumed the auction. Although Zeng Yilong objected to this, he participated in the subsequent auction activities and raised his paddle to bid when the auctioneer quoted RMB 27.15 million. This should be deemed as his acceptance of the auctioneer's correction of the error. The auctioneer's first hammer fall in this case was a mistake. His oral declaration that Zeng Yilong purchased the auction subject matter at RMB 26.7 million had no legal effect. Zeng Yilong's request that the court declare the first hammer fall valid and order the company to issue a confirmation of sale for RMB 26.7 million lacked legal basis and should be dismissed. Since Zeng Yilong's above claim could not be supported, his request for a declaration that the second hammer fall was invalid and for the revocation of Jinma Company's Auction Sale Confirmation lacked factual basis and was not adopted. Although Zeng Yilong's claims were not supported, this dispute was caused by the negligence of Jinma Company's auctioneer, and Jinma Company should bear part of the litigation costs. Accordingly, following discussion and decision by the Judicial Committee of the Jiangxi High People's Court, and pursuant to Article 6, Article 50(2), and Article 52 of the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China, it was adjudicated that Zeng Yilong's claims were dismissed. The court fee for first instance was RMB 143,510, with Zeng Yilong bearing RMB 86,106 and Jinma Company bearing RMB 57,404.

Zeng Yilong, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to this Court, requesting: 1. Reversal of Civil Judgment (2004) Gan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 4; 2. Amendment to confirm that the appellant purchased part of the property rights of "Zhengda Commercial Building" in Shangrao City at RMB 26.7 million in the auction conducted by Jinma Company on May 12, 2004, and that Jinma Company immediately issue a confirmation of sale to the appellant; 3. Confirmation that the second hammer fall (RMB 27.4 million) for "Zhengda Commercial Building" by the auctioneer in the auction of Jinma Company on May 12, 2004, was invalid, and that the Auction Sale Confirmation signed between Jinma Company and Xu Wei was invalid; 4. Jinma Company to bear all court costs for both first and second instances. His main reasons were: First, the video recording of the auction site showed that after three calls for RMB 21 million, no one other than Bidder No. 12 responded. The auctioneer again asked if anyone would increase the bid, and then told Bidder No. 12 that his bid did not reach the reserve price, asking, "RMB 26.7 million, do you want it?" Bidder No. 12 raised his paddle and responded. The auctioneer thanked him and dropped the hammer, declaring the auction concluded, ending the auction. This process showed that the auctioneer satisfied the bidding rights of all bidders at the RMB 21 million quotation. A bid is an offer, and the auctioneer's hammer fall is an acceptance. After the hammer falls, the auction contract is established, and neither party may unilaterally rescind the contract. Second, the first-instance judgment's finding that "three quotations should be made both before and after" had no legal basis. The first-instance judgment found that the "three-call quotation method" is a customary technical measure in China's auction market, with no specific legal provisions. Since there are no legal provisions or provisions in the Auction Rules, and the auctioneer did not mention it in the auction precautions, it cannot be used as a basis for determining the validity of the auction actions. Third, the first-instance judgment's finding that "the auctioneer's first hammer fall was a mistake" had no legal basis. Since other bidders did not respond to the RMB 21 million quotation and no one increased the bid after further inquiry, legally, these persons had abandoned their bidding rights. Logically, if they did not respond to a lower quotation, anyone would have reason to believe that bidders other than Bidder No. 12 would not bid at a higher price. The view that "because other bidders raised objections, the auctioneer recognized his mistake and resumed the auction, and although Zeng Yilong objected, he participated in the subsequent auction and raised his paddle to bid at RMB 27.15 million, which should be deemed as acceptance of the auctioneer's correction" was untenable. The appellant never accepted the auctioneer's second auction and protested on the spot, seeking intervention from government regulatory authorities. An auction is a strictly procedural activity. Even if the first hammer fall was indeed a mistake, the auction company should bear compensation liability to the injured party, not invalidate the auction action and cause the bidder to bear the consequences of the auction company's "mistake." Fourth, the first-instance judgment's finding that the second hammer fall was valid was manifestly unfair and lacked legal basis. According to auction procedures, after the auctioneer's first hammer fall and declaration of conclusion, the auction activity should end. No one has the right to unilaterally deny the validity of the acceptance. Organizing a continued auction under these circumstances and finding the second auction valid disrupts normal market order and harms the appellant's lawful rights.

The appellee Jinma Company, the original third party Shangrao Branch of Bank of China, and the original third party Xu Shengju responded, requesting that the first-instance judgment be upheld.

The appellee Jinma Company argued that the key to determining the conclusion of an auction is to confirm whether there has been a highest bid and a purchase, not whether the hammer has fallen. The hammer fall is a form of confirming the highest bid and purchase and thus the conclusion of the auction, not the purchase or the auction conclusion itself. Whether the hammer fall has the effect of confirming the auction conclusion depends on whether a highest bid has occurred and whether the legal fact of purchase has occurred. The evidence in this case showed that when a bid of RMB 26.7 million appeared, before all other bidders had publicly indicated whether they had a new bid, the auctioneer dropped the hammer and declared the auction concluded. Subsequently, other bidders immediately raised objections, and the auctioneer promptly corrected the error by withdrawing the invalid acceptance. Since RMB 26.7 million was not the highest bid, the auctioneer's withdrawal protected the rights of all bidders and should be confirmed. After the new round of bidding, through 10 rounds of bids up to RMB 27.4 million, including the appellant, all bidders retained the right to continue public bidding, but none made a bid indication. After confirming this as the highest price, the auctioneer dropped the hammer to confirm the auction conclusion, and the buyer immediately signed the Auction Sale Confirmation. Therefore, this auction was fair, lawful, and valid. Auction activities must follow the principles of public bidding and the highest bidder wins. A bidder does not automatically lose the right to participate in bidding again just because he did not bid at a certain price level. If a bidder who did not bid at RMB 21 million is deprived of the right to bid again at RMB 26.7 million, the auction would violate the basic spirit of the Auction Law to protect and encourage public bidding.

The original third party Shangrao Branch of Bank of China responded that, as the mortgagee of "Zhengda Commercial Building," it entrusted Jinma Company to auction the property pursuant to the Civil Ruling (2003) Rao Zhong Zhi Zi No. 35 of the Shangrao Intermediate People's Court to realize its creditor's rights. This act was lawful and valid.

The original third party Xu Shengju argued that his successful bid at the highest price of RMB 27.4 million was a civil jural act fully in accordance with the law and should be protected by law.

The second instance of this Court found: On May 10, 2005, the original third party Bank of China Limited officially commenced using the seal "Shangrao Branch of Bank of China Limited," and the former seal "Bank of China Shangrao Branch" was simultaneously abolished. On May 30, 2005, Zeng Yilong retrieved the RMB 2 million deposit bond that Jinma Company had deposited with the Xinzhou District Notary Office of Shangrao City.

The second instance of this Court further found: On the afternoon of May 12, 2004, during the auction of part of the property rights of "Zhengda Commercial Building" by Jinma Company, when Bidder No. 12 bid RMB 21 million and the auctioneer made three calls with no other response, the auctioneer asked Bidder No. 12: "No. 12, your increase did not reach the reserve price. RMB 26.7 million, do you want it?" Bidder No. 12 raised his paddle and said "Bid." The auctioneer said, "Thank you!" and then dropped the hammer, declaring: "No. 12 won the part of the real estate rights of Zhengda Commercial Building at RMB 26.7 million. Good! Today's auction of the subject matter is concluded."

During the second instance, the appellee Jinma Company submitted as new evidence a letter from the Shangrao Branch of Bank of China dated May 12, 2004, addressed to Jinma Company, regarding the reserve price of the entrusted auction subject matter and the disclosure of the reserve price. The appellant Zeng Yilong argued during cross-examination that this evidence did not fall within the scope of new evidence under the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Procedures. Since Jinma Company failed to submit this evidence in the first instance, the court of second instance should not accept it as new evidence.

Other facts found by this Court are the same as those of the first instance.

This Court holds: The focus of the dispute between the parties in the second instance is which hammer fall, at RMB 26.7 million or RMB 27.4 million, was valid during the auction of part of the property rights of "Zhengda Commercial Building" by Jinma Company on behalf of the Shangrao Branch of Bank of China on May 12, 2004. According to the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China, and with reference to the Auction Rules provided by Jinma Company to all bidders and the customary practices of the auction industry, during the auction of part of the property rights of "Zhengda Commercial Building" by Jinma Company, both the hammer falls at RMB 26.7 million and RMB 27.4 million by the auctioneer were invalid.

The main reasons for finding the first hammer fall at RMB 26.7 million invalid are: First, an auction is a method of sale that transfers specific items or property rights to the highest bidder through public bidding. During the auction of part of the property rights of "Zhengda Commercial Building" by Jinma Company, when the auctioneer quoted RMB 21 million, no one other than Bidder No. 12 responded, and the reserve price of "Zhengda Commercial Building" was RMB 26.7 million. According to Article 50(2) of the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China: "If the auction subject matter has a reserve price and the highest bid does not reach the reserve price, that bid is invalid and the auctioneer shall stop the auction of the subject matter." At that time, although the auctioneer did not declare the end of the auction in accordance with the law, objectively, a failed auction had already occurred, and the RMB 21 million bid of Bidder No. 12 was invalid. Second, auction activities are civil jural acts with strict procedural requirements. According to the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China and industry practices, the auctioneer should publicly quote to all bidders at the auction site, continue to increase the price based on bids, and drop the hammer to declare the auction concluded when a highest bid appears. After declaring that Bidder No. 12's RMB 21 million bid did not reach the reserve price, the auctioneer of Jinma Company did not declare a failed auction but instead inquired solely of Bidder No. 12 whether he would accept the reserve price of RMB 26.7 million, and upon his agreement, dropped the hammer and declared the auction concluded. The above practice of Jinma Company's auctioneer, because it did not follow the principle of quoting to all bidders, a principle that auction activities must adhere to, violated the principle of fairness and impartiality, infringed on the legitimate rights of other bidders to participate in bidding fairly, and objectively failed to maximize the principal's interests. Third, the so-called "three-call quotation method" is one of the traditional quotation methods in the auction industry and is still recognized by many auction companies and bidders in China. Whether this auction must adopt the "three-call quotation method" is not stipulated in the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China nor in Jinma Company's Auction Rules. However, the auctioneer of Jinma Company used the "three-call quotation method" for quotations prior to RMB 26.7 million, and the bidders at the site accepted this quotation method. This indicates that the customary practice of three-call quotation had become a rule that must be followed in this auction. The auctioneer's act of dropping the hammer and declaring the auction concluded without making three calls at the RMB 26.7 million price violated the rules of this auction and also deprived other bidders of the opportunity to participate fairly in the bidding. Therefore, the hammer fall at RMB 26.7 million by Jinma Company's auctioneer was invalid.

The main reasons for finding the second hammer fall at RMB 27.4 million invalid are: "Zhengda Commercial Building" was an auction subject matter with a reserve price. When the highest bid of RMB 21 million did not reach the reserve price, according to the Auction Law of the People's Republic of China, "the auctioneer shall stop the auction of the subject matter." If the reserve price is disclosed and a new auction is to be held, a new announcement should be made and, in accordance with industry practice, the reserve price should be lowered. However, in practice, some auction companies do not end the auction after a failed auction but continue the auction. This practice is not prohibited by law. After the failed auction, Jinma Company's auctioneer made a separate quotation to Bidder No. 12 and dropped the hammer, declaring that the latter had purchased part of the property rights of "Zhengda Commercial Building" at RMB 26.7 million. Due to protests from other bidders, he then continued the auction based on this price. The bidder Zeng Yilong, who had been informed by the auctioneer that he had won the bid at RMB 26.7 million, immediately protested. The auctioneer of Jinma Company did not provide a reasonable explanation or properly handle the hammer fall at RMB 26.7 million but instead continued the auction activities. Although Zeng Yilong, after failing to stop the subsequent auction, also raised his paddle to bid, the auctioneer of Jinma Company did not address the dispute that had already arisen at the auction site. Instead, he violated auction procedures by continuing the auction and lightly denying his already-made declaration of the hammer fall constituting the conclusion, which caused the bidder Zeng Yilong to lose the normal mindset and judgment to continue participating in fair bidding along with other bidders. Therefore, the subsequent auction activities were unfair to Zeng Yilong. Second, after the hammer fell at RMB 26.7 million, the auctioneer of Jinma Company immediately declared, "Today's auction of the subject matter is concluded." The entire auction process had ended. If the disputed subject matter required a new auction, Jinma Company should have organized a separate auction. Continuing the auction based on the price of RMB 26.7 million did not comply with auction rules. The auction conduct from RMB 26.7 million to RMB 27.4 million constituted an invalid civil jural act. Therefore, the hammer fall at RMB 27.4 million by Jinma Company's auctioneer was also invalid.

Zeng Yilong appealed arguing that the hammer fall at the price of RMB 26.7 million was valid, raising several reasons: first, the bidder's bid constituted an offer, and the auctioneer's hammer fall constituted an acceptance; after the hammer fall, the auction contract was concluded, and neither party could unilaterally rescind the contract. This Court holds that for a contract to be lawfully concluded, the so-called "lawful" means that both the offer and acceptance must be lawful. The law has special provisions on the offer and acceptance in an auction contract. The auctioneer of Jinma Company, before bringing the hammer down at the price of RMB 26.7 million, did not publicly announce the bid to all bidders, nor did he conduct three calls for bids, thereby violating the statutory procedures for auction activities and the basic principles of openness and fairness under the Auction Law. His act of hammer fall constituted an invalid acceptance. The sales contract between Zeng Yilong and Jinma Company was not lawfully concluded, and therefore the issue of rescission of contract does not arise. Second, there is no legal provision for the "three-call bidding method" in auction activities, nor is it stipulated in the auction rules, nor was it explained by the auctioneer in the auction matters; thus it cannot be used as a basis for determining the validity of the auction act. This Court holds that the "three-call bidding method" is a practice in the auction industry. In the auction involved in this case, this bidding method was adopted from the very beginning and was accepted by all bidders, including Zeng Yilong. Although the law and auction rules do not provide for such a bidding method, an industry practice that is recognized by all parties in a specific civil activity has legally binding force, and the parties in this auction activity must comply with it. The auctioneer of Jinma Company did not call the bid three times when quoting the price of RMB 26.7 million, thereby violating the procedural rules for auction activities and also infringing upon the rights of other bidders. Therefore, Zeng Yilong's claim that a single bid call followed by a hammer fall is valid lacks legal basis. Third, the other bidders did not respond to the bid of RMB 21 million, which means they had given up their bidding rights, including the right to bid at prices above RMB 21 million. This Court holds that after three calls at the price of RMB 21 million, the bidders' failure to respond merely indicates that they gave up their bidding rights at that price. If, due to the reserve price not being met, no transaction was concluded at that price, it should be considered a no-sale. If the auction continues, it should be deemed a new round of auction, and bidders who did not respond at the price of RMB 21 million still retain the right to bid at new higher prices. Zeng Yilong's denial of other bidders' right to bid at prices above RMB 21 million has no legal basis. Therefore, the court of first instance held that the auctioneer of Jinma Company, by individually inquiring with Zeng Yilong at the price of RMB 26.7 million and bringing the hammer down after a single bid call to declare the auction concluded, acted in violation of the basic principles of the Auction Law of the PRC, infringed upon the interests of other bidders, and failed to maximize the interests of the principal. The oral declaration by Jinma Company's auctioneer that Zeng Yilong had purchased the subject matter at the price of RMB 26.7 million is not legally valid, and this finding was not erroneous. Zeng Yilong's appeal request that the hammer fall at the price of RMB 26.7 million be upheld is not supported by this Court.

Zeng Yilong appealed arguing that the hammer fall at the price of RMB 27.4 million was invalid, with the main reason being that after the auctioneer first brought the hammer down to declare the transaction concluded, he should have declared the auction ended and had no right to unilaterally negate the validity of the acceptance and continue to organize the auction. Upholding the second hammer fall as valid would disrupt normal market order. The court of first instance held that the auctioneer of Jinma Company had clearly acted improperly by bringing the hammer down at the price of RMB 26.7 million, and after recognizing his mistake, he restarted the auction. When the price was quoted at RMB 27.15 million, Zeng Yilong raised his paddle to bid, which should be regarded as his acceptance of the auctioneer's correction of the error. Regarding the issue of whether an auctioneer can correct his own errors, including illegal acts, during an auction, this Court holds that neither the Auction Law of the PRC nor Jinma Company's Auction Rules contain provisions on this matter. Whether an auctioneer has the right to correct his errors in an auction should not be categorically denied or affirmed, but should be determined based on the specific circumstances. The basic requirement for self-correction of errors is that it must not violate the basic principles of fairness and openness under the Auction Law, must not violate auction procedures, and must not harm the lawful rights and interests of others. From the specific auction activity involved in this case, a dispute arose between other bidders and Zeng Yilong regarding the hammer fall at RMB 26.7 million. This dispute was caused by the irregular conduct of Jinma Company's auctioneer. Without providing a reasonable explanation and proper handling, the auctioneer declared the hammer fall invalid and continued the auction, which was inconsistent with the principles of openness and fairness in auctions. After declaring the conclusion of this auction, the auctioneer proceeded to continue the auction, violating auction procedures. When there is a dispute among bidders over a hammer fall, and the auctioneer is unable to explain and handle it properly, he has no right to unilaterally declare the hammer fall invalid; rather, the validity of the hammer fall should be confirmed through lawful means. After the auction has been declared concluded, the auctioneer's act of "self-correcting" by continuing the auction, regardless of whether Zeng Yilong participated, violates auction procedures. In summary, Zeng Yilong's appeal argument that the hammer fall at RMB 27.4 million was invalid is justified, and this Court supports it. The first-instance judgment's dismissal of Zeng Yilong's claim that the hammer fall at RMB 27.4 million was invalid was erroneous, and this Court hereby corrects it.

Since the appellant Zeng Yilong, during both the first and second instances of this case, consistently insisted on the claim that the hammer fall by Jinma Company's auctioneer at the price of RMB 26.7 million on May 12, 2004, was valid, and did not raise any specific claim for damages regarding the invalidity of that hammer fall, the issues of whether losses exist and whether compensation should be awarded are not within the scope of review of this second instance.

This Court has upheld part of Zeng Yilong's appeal requests. In accordance with the general principles on the allocation of litigation costs, the case acceptance fees in this case shall be borne by Zeng Yilong and Jinma Company. However, the dispute in this case was caused by the improper conduct of Jinma Company, which bears primary responsibility; therefore, Jinma Company shall bear a greater portion of the case acceptance fees. Pursuant to Article 173 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Article 4 of the Auction Law of the PRC, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment (2004) Gan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 4 of the Jiangxi High People's Court;

2. The auction by Jiangxi Jinma Auction Co., Ltd. of part of the property rights of the "Zhengda Commercial Building" on the afternoon of May 12, 2004, is invalid;

3. Dismiss the other appeal requests of Zeng Yilong.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 143,510 shall be borne by Zeng Yilong in the amount of RMB 28,702, and by Jiangxi Jinma Auction Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 114,808. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 143,510 shall be borne by the appellant Zeng Yilong in the amount of RMB 28,702, and by the appellee Jiangxi Jinma Auction Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 114,808.

This judgment is final.
